subject: Setting a covariate prior in a proportional hazards model

messages.author: e697cf3756e4cc61
messages.subject: Setting a covariate prior in a proportional hazards model
parts:
Hi,

I am looking to set a prior on covariate in a proportional hazards model. Based on the following examples, I am not sure I understand how the prior influences the covariate effect estimate. I adapted some code from the Bayesian inference with INLA book (https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/inla-gitbook/ch-survival.html#semi-parametric-estimation-cox-proportional-hazards) below.  With no fixed effect prior, the model reports mean = -0.047 and sd = 0.179 for trt. Changing the mean between 1, -1, 10, and -10 with a constant precision (of 10 for example) on the prior resulted in consistent estimates for trt. Increasing the precision would increase the estimate closer to 0, and decrease the standard deviation. Am I missing something here? Thanks so much.

veteran$time.m <- round(veteran$time / 30, 3)
sinla.vet <- inla.surv(veteran$time.m, veteran$status)

# No trt prior
coxinla.vet <- inla(sinla.vet ~  1 + trt, data = veteran,
                    family = "coxph",
                    control.hazard = list(hyper = list(prec = list(param = c(0.001, 0.001)))))
summary(coxinla.vet) # beta <- -0.047 (+/-0.179)

# Prior on trt - change mean and precision as needed
coxinla.vet2 <- inla(sinla.vet ~ 1   + trt, data = veteran,
                    family = "coxph",
                    control.hazard = list(hyper = list(prec = list(param = c(0.001, 0.001)))),
                    control.fixed = list(mean = list(trt = 1), prec = list(trt=10)))
summary(coxinla.vet2)

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Setting a covariate prior in a proportional hazards model
parts:
I would use

control.hazard = list(hyper = list(
prec = list(prior="pc.prec,
param = c(0.5, 0.01)))

see the 'penalized complexity prior'-paper in statistical science.

I don't think you need to change the mean for 'trt'. you can check the
results with various precisions, for it. I guess 'trt' is binary, right?
so that you would not expect to much impact of changing trt from 0 to 1,
and an estimate of that ratio, should give you an approximate precision
for the prior. I would guess that prec=10 would be about ok, but you
might also try with prec=1 (which is very vague)

Thanks. I have similar problems. I have exactly the same setting as Arlene has above. I am trying to put a prior on the estimated treatment effect using

I am also trying to see how different priors would impact my results, so I tried different values for mean param but kept prec as the same. Then, I ran the INLA survival model. The point estimates (posterior means) were the same regardless how I change the mean param? I would expect the posterior means to be somehow different if I changed the prior means. However, it seems not to be the case. Did I miss anything here? 
Many thanks,
Derek
